title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files

reading.body:
This incident shows a general-purpose AI coding and agent tool being used as an operational component in active ransomware attacks. The Aurora operator directed Cursor Agent, which runs on Claude Sonnet, to carry out hands-on exploitation against target organizations. The tool was not subverted or jailbroken in any way that the reporting describes, it was simply used by a malicious actor as a capable assistant for tasks the tool was built to perform, such as writing and executing code. This is a misuse failure, not a model hallucination or impersonation, and it occurred entirely within normal deployment conditions.

The failure is located at the access layer of the product. A sufficiently capable agentic tool used without meaningful checks on who is operating it or toward what end becomes available to any actor who can obtain an account. The attack chain also included a custom Python scanning tool, suggesting the AI assistance was one component among several, not the sole enabler. What might have caught this is behavioral monitoring of agent sessions for patterns consistent with reconnaissance or exploitation, though whether such monitoring exists or was feasible is not established by the reporting.

It is not established that Anysphere, the company behind Cursor, was aware of this use, that any terms-of-service enforcement occurred, or that the attacks attributed to Aurora have resulted in any legal findings against identified individuals. The attribution to Russian-speaking cybercriminals and the victim count come from researcher reports, not from law enforcement findings or court proceedings.

reports.title: Russian-speaking cybercriminals used SpaceX’s Cursor AI tool to hack seven companies
Aurora ransomware targets ESXi, abuses Cursor Agent for exploitation

summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that Aurora ransomware, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual machine environments. The group operates a data leak site and has victimized organizations across multiple countries. Researchers identified the Aurora operator using Cursor Agent, an AI tool running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation attacks against ten target organizations between April 8 and May 21, 2026. The Linux ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption with RSA-4096 key wrapping and includes an ESXi mode that terminates running virtual machines before encrypting their files while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can read ransom demands.

The investigation also revealed a custom scanning tool called esxi_finder.py that identifies ESXi hypervisors and vCenter servers on victim networks by scanning ports 443 and 902. Researchers identified a second Aurora cluster, attributed with medium confidence, that used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation and S3 bucket exfiltration across eight victim organizations in Israel, Germany, Austria, Spain, the United States, and Argentina. The findings include technical indicators of compromise, IP addresses, and domains associated with both attack clusters.
